note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Find an open, airy spring panicle with distinct oval spikelets, then trace the SAME perennial plant back to its basal rosette. Seasonal leafy autumn branches can look different. Existing photos show actual branching and spikelets but do not establish a connected winter rosette or measured anatomy.
tiles.short: Open spring panicle PLUS rooted winter rosette
tiles.status: PANICLE PHOTO PRESENT; MATCHED ROOTED ROSETTE MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE COLLAR
tiles.details: At the INSIDE blade–sheath junction inspect the actual fringe of hairs; published descriptions vary by taxon treatment, roughly 1–4.2 mm (about 1–3 mm in a narrower treatment). Separate ligule hairs from leaf-edge cilia and sheath hairs. A 1-mm ruler and side-lit 10–20× macro are required for an anatomical arrow.
tiles.short: True hair-fringe ligule commonly about 1–4 mm
tiles.status: PUBLISHED RANGE; TRUE LIGULE MACRO MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE THREE RIPE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Measure at least three mature spikelets from one source-verified plant; Kew describes 2.9–4-mm-long, 1.2–2.2-mm-wide awnless spikelets. An open panicle without a scale cannot distinguish this species from D. pedicellatum. Each spikelet has a lower sterile and upper fertile floret.
tiles.status: LITERATURE SIZE; MEASURED ATTACHED SPIKELETS MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · FIND BOTH GLUMES
tiles.details: Kew's broad species treatment gives a LOWER glume about 0.8–2.2 mm (roughly one-quarter to one-half the spikelet), with 1–3 veins, and an UPPER glume about as long as the spikelet with about five veins. Do not label upper glume or vein counts unless the photographed bract is actually separated and in focus. Narrow subspecies descriptions can give smaller lower-glume ranges.
tiles.short: Lower glume about 0.8–2.2 mm; upper near full length
tiles.status: PUBLISHED GLUME RANGES; DISSECTION/VEIN ARROWS MISSING

tiles.heading: 05 · OPEN THE TWO FLORETS
tiles.details: The lower sterile lemma resembles the upper glume and is approximately spikelet-length with about five veins; a reduced sterile palea may be present. The UPPER fertile lemma is hardened and approximately 2.9–4 mm in Kew's broad treatment, with a firm palea inside. Both florets are AWNLESS. Dissect one mature spikelet and show each bract separately before drawing labels.
tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma thin; upper fertile lemma hardened
tiles.status: LITERATURE ANATOMY; INDIVIDUAL LEMMA PHOTOS MISSING

tiles.heading: 06 · RULE OUT NEARBY DICHANTHELIUM
tiles.details: D. pedicellatum overlaps in spikelet size (roughly 3–3.5 mm) but the Williamson County treatment describes a small cormlike base, no winter rosette, and a very short 0.25–0.5-mm hair ligule. D. lindheimeri usually has much smaller ripe spikelets (about 1.3–1.7 mm); D. commutatum may have broad heart-based leaves and a minute or absent true ligule. Use the same plant's rooted base, collar and ripe spikelets together.
tiles.short: Pedicellatum overlaps; measure ligule and base
tiles.status: COMPARISONS WRITTEN; MATCHED ORGAN PHOTOS MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: FEW-FLOWERED PANICGRASS: recognize the rather OPEN spring flowering panicle and many separate small oval spikelets, then locate the broader winter basal ROSETTE on the same rooted clump and measure ripe spikelets (~2.9–4 mm). Existing photo really shows panicle and oval units, NOT size/ligule. A hair-fringe ligule usually longer than tiny pedicellatum's ~0.25–0.5 mm must be photographed under scale.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START panel 11 (index 10): true Max Licher D. oligosanthes living plant with a clump of leafy stems and several small flowering axes. Stem bases are seen at SOIL but roots and caudex are NOT uncovered.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: At the INSIDE blade–sheath junction inspect the actual fringe of hairs; published descriptions vary by taxon treatment, roughly 1–4.2 mm (about 1–3 mm in a narrower treatment). Separate ligule hairs from leaf-edge cilia and sheath hairs. A 1-mm ruler and side-lit 10–20× macro are required for an anatomical arrow.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Measure at least three mature spikelets from one source-verified plant; Kew describes 2.9–4-mm-long, 1.2–2.2-mm-wide awnless spikelets. An open panicle without a scale cannot distinguish this species from D. pedicellatum. Each spikelet has a lower sterile and upper fertile floret.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Compared with D. lindheimeri, ripe spikelets are much larger (~2.9–4 vs 1.3–1.6 mm); compared with D. pedicellatum (~3–3.5 mm), lengths overlap and true collar fringe plus leaf widths are critical. D. commutatum may have broad/cordate stem blade bases and minute/absent true ligule. Don't force the identity from one branching inflorescence.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: Few-flowered panicgrass — verified original field photo
panels.caption: Existing photograph clearly shows a branching OPEN panicle, very slender flowering pedicels and separate green oval attached spikelets on a fine central axis. It is a good panicle-shape lesson but contains NO measured 2.9–4 mm size, crown, collar or sheath-hair information.
panels.creator: Choess
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: FEW-FLOWERED PANICGRASS — real archived spikelet close-up
panels.caption: Jschnable's close-up displays real photographed spikelets. Learn their arrangement; inspect fresh spikelets under magnification before assigning glume veins or measured organ positions.
panels.creator: Jschnable
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: Variable panicgrass — verified original field photo
panels.caption: Actual original close-up visibly shows dark violet hanging ANTHERS, two red feathery STIGMA branches, and a green hairy spikelet body. It does NOT show the diagnostic broad/cordate leaf base, true ligule, panicle architecture or precise 2.1–3.2 mm size.
panels.creator: Alexander Abair
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

intro: FEW-FLOWERED PANICGRASS: recognize the rather OPEN spring flowering panicle and many separate small oval spikelets, then locate the broader winter basal ROSETTE on the same rooted clump and measure ripe spikelets (~2.9–4 mm). Existing photo really shows panicle and oval units, NOT size/ligule. A hair-fringe ligule usually longer than tiny pedicellatum's ~0.25–0.5 mm must be photographed under scale.
memory_rule: ROSETTE + LEAF BASE + TRUE COLLAR → THREE MEASURED SPIKELETS. 1.3–1.6 LIN; 2.1–3.2 COM; 2.9–4 OLI; 3–3.5 PED (mm; OLI/PED overlap).
safety_note: Own-species photographs now 8 (one historical illustration stored separately), 12 teaching panels, and seven new arrows on 3 Arizona photos. Real inner hair fringe, exposed caudex/roots and scale-confirmed detached glume/lemma remain unphotographed; species source identification does not independently authenticate Hays specimens.
field_rule: Panicles often overlap. Show spring/autumn phase, true leaf collar, and at least three mature measured spikelets from the same plant before a firm species call.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
